content: Dicloxacillin sodium is an antibacterial agent that belongs to the isoxazolyl penicillin class. It is a semisynthetic penicillin that is resistant to penicillinase and stable in acidic environments, making it suitable for oral administration. This medication exerts a bactericidal effect by targeting penicillin-susceptible microorganisms, specifically during their active multiplication phase. Dicloxacillin sodium has demonstrated efficacy against most strains of aerobic gram-positive microorganisms, including penicillinase-producing Staphylococcus species. It is categorized as a penicillinase-resistant penicillin. The mechanism of action of penicillinase-resistant penicillins, such as dicloxacillin, involves the inhibition of bacterial cell wall biosynthesis. This disruption of cell wall synthesis ultimately leads to the death of actively multiplying bacteria.
